title: Two branches start on the same file unnoticed
what: Before a new branch starts, one relay command lists the open wt/* branches that already change any of the files the brief names (from relay changed --own of each open branch against the default branch), so the front starts a branch only when its files are free or says why not; the delegate skill names the step.
why: Owner, 26 Oct: "агенты позволяют нам делать множество изменений одновременно, большие файлы - наши враги, концентрируя большой объем кода (смысла) они являются поводом для конфликтов", then "a" (principle 10 "one subject per file, no hub files, no copies" plus four items). Measured over 5 days: bin/relay (887 lines) in 44 commits, lib/relay_queue.py (1189 lines) in 25 commits kept in 3 copies, lib/relay_setup.py (1134 lines) changed by 3 open branches at once (license, setup-wt, the portable-tool design). IP chosen by the front (agent-chosen). 26 Oct live: wt/where-list's rewrite of every queue record met master's changes to the same records and stopped in a conflict; R4 and R5 of the pilot wait by hand because their files are taken.
failing_case: Two worktrees on branches that both change lib/relay_setup.py: nothing in relay says so before the second one starts.
pass_cases: The new command, given lib/relay_setup.py, names the open branch that changes it; given a free file it says free; it reads only git, writes nothing.
where: bin/relay (a new subcommand or relay changed)
